method_description: How GPU prices are collected and compared on {date} UTC: {count}, {models}, {regions}. USD list rates, GPU shares, Spot and history.
method_api: Verified public sources: tier A official APIs, including {source}, may be displayed and exported. B/C pages are display only, fetched at most once per hour per provider. JSON includes only tier A rows with export_allowed. Link-only sources are never fetched.
method_filters: We request Virtual Machines in NC, ND and NV families across all commercial regions with USD currency, Consumption prices and primary meters. Windows, paid Linux license add-ons, Dev/Test, reservations, savings plans, legacy Low Priority, non-hourly, future-effective, zero-price and invalid meters are excluded. Base VM products without a Windows designation are treated as Linux base-OS list rates.
method_mapping: Known exact ARM SKUs map to documented GPU model, GPU count, vCPU and RAM. Unknown SKUs and conflicting same-date rates are logged and skipped. The most recent effective date wins within a collection. L40S and other unverified sizes are not guessed. Curated coverage is not exhaustive.
method_units: FX uses dated ECB reference rates: EUR × USD rate, or CNY × USD rate / CNY rate. Failed refreshes retain the last valid date. Original currency and hourly price remain visible. Monthly prices are never divided into hourly prices.
method_exclusions: Minimum, median and maximum use current, exact USD prices for whole GPUs across all providers, separately for on-demand and Spot. Standard and unspecified regions are eligible; edge and restricted regions are excluded. Unknown tax basis is eligible and labelled; tax-included, fractional, GPU-component-only and advertised starting prices are excluded. GPU-hour rates divide instance rates by GPU count; per-GPU rates retain their scope. Calculations use unrounded values. Minima may refer to different regions or SKUs. Region counts include an unspecified-location group when present. Verda uses public instance types and separate on-demand and Spot fields. Regions and live stock are unknown. CPU core semantics and RAM byte convention are unverified, so their original descriptions are shown. No authenticated availability endpoint is queried.
method_history: Daily history retains the latest observed rate per provider, SKU, region and price type. Minimum, median with sample count and maximum use the same eligible whole-GPU population as headlines, including unspecified regions, with on-demand and Spot kept separate. Missing days are not filled and stale providers are excluded from today. Coverage changes affect the series.
method_snapshot: Stale · latest fetch failed or is from an earlier day. Cheapest among observed offers only. Coverage depends on the last collection; this is not a global-market minimum.
method_network: HTTP uses approved HTTPS endpoints and refuses redirects, without credentials, cookies or browser impersonation. APIs use backoff and Retry-After. Page requests have no automatic retries; every attempt, including failure, consumes the persisted hourly budget. HTTP 403 stops the source.
affiliates: Some links may be affiliate links. This does not affect rankings or prices shown. Provider-only cards carry no scraped price and are excluded from every comparison.
not_found_description: The requested page does not exist. Choose a language to browse observed GPU prices.
basis: Minimum, median and maximum use current, exact USD prices for whole GPUs across all providers, separately for on-demand and Spot. Standard and unspecified regions are eligible; edge and restricted regions are excluded. Unknown tax basis is eligible and labelled; tax-included, fractional, GPU-component-only and advertised starting prices are excluded. GPU-hour rates divide instance rates by GPU count; per-GPU rates retain their scope. Calculations use unrounded values. Minima may refer to different regions or SKUs. Region counts include an unspecified-location group when present.

region_chart_desc: Paired horizontal bars compare on-demand and Spot minima within each eligible region. Missing bars mean no observed price. Labels give the exact displayed values.

faq_cheapest_q: What is the lowest observed {model} rental price?
faq_cheapest_a: On-demand: {demand}/GPU-hour. Spot: {spot}/GPU-hour. Separate observed minima across {regions} eligible location groups and {offers} whole-GPU offers on {date} UTC; unspecified locations are included. Capacity and quota are not guaranteed.
faq_spot_q: How does Spot compare with on-demand?
faq_spot_a: {comparison} Spot can be interrupted. The two minimum prices may refer to different regions or SKUs.
faq_units_q: Does this rental price cover a whole GPU?
faq_units_a: Headline offers use whole GPUs. Cards show the GPU count, instance-hour price and per-GPU-hour price. GPU-component-only rates are labelled separately. Fractional offers show their share and full-GPU-equivalent rate in a separate list.
method_regions: Offers in edge and restricted regions stay visible with badges but do not enter headline comparisons or history. An unspecified region is eligible and labelled “Region not specified by provider”. Unrecognized region IDs default to standard and are logged for review. Restricted badges include sovereign clouds and the conservative exclusion of West India and legacy Jio regions.
method_rounding: Dollar values use two decimals at or above USD 1 and three decimals below USD 1, using unrounded source values for all calculations. Counts n accompany every offer-price median. No discount percentage is displayed when the Spot minimum is at least the on-demand minimum; discounts are never negative.
method_cadence: The workflow may run every 15 minutes; each page provider is fetched at most once per rolling hour. SQLite meta persists the time across runs. Skips retain the observation and collection status. UTC dates and outcomes indicate freshness; missing history days are not filled.
method_audit: Every build independently recalculates published prices and statistics from SQLite, checks JSON exports and localized HTML including titles, descriptions, FAQ structured data and charts, and fails on a mismatch. Optional live sampling compares stored VM prices with Azure; a newer effective date is reported as a source update rather than a historical error.
maximum_def: Maximum = the highest price across the same eligible offers. Models tracked = the number of distinct GPU models represented in today's eligible offers.

growth_data_intro: Language-neutral JSON exports contain Tier A, export-allowed records only. B/C display-only and provider-restricted data are excluded, including from statistics and history.
growth_cadence: Refresh is scheduled every 15 minutes. Unchanged data may reuse a build for up to six hours. Provider request budgets, failures and source changes can delay updates. Observation timestamps describe source checks; generated_at describes a build, not a new observation.
growth_license: Our rights in the compiled data are licensed under CC BY 4.0. Provider content, trademarks and other third-party rights are excluded; this licence does not grant rights we do not hold.
growth_attribution: Credit GPU Price Index and link to this data page and the licence. Indicate any changes and retain source and observation dates. Attribution does not imply endorsement. No warranty of price or availability.
growth_fields_top: Top-level fields identify the exact model, currency, UTC observation day, latest observed time, build time, source URLs, collection status, offers, statistics and history. Missing facts are null; arrays may be empty.
growth_fields_prices: Prices retain their scope and billing basis. price_per_hour is hourly in that scope; price_per_gpu_hour requires an explicit allocation. Monthly commitments are excluded; original day rates are retained where applicable.
growth_fields_hardware: Hardware fields retain provider, SKU, model, allocation, location and raw source descriptions. ram_gb uses GiB; unknown hardware or locations stay null. Explicit model and memory variants remain distinct.
growth_fields_policy: Policy fields retain price type, currency, tier/export permission, tax basis, promotional conditions and observed availability. A listed offer does not guarantee stock. Only eligible whole-GPU USD rows enter comparisons, separated by price type.
growth_fields_time: Provenance fields retain source and UTC check/effective times. Original amounts and dated ECB exchange-rate inputs remain available; native currencies without conversion stay outside USD statistics.
growth_fields_stats: Statistics use unweighted eligible offers. History stores observed daily group minima and distributions by price type; missing days are not filled. Historical group counts are not counts of all marketplace hosts.
growth_feed_rules: Up to 50 notable changes from the last 30 UTC days, using Tier A eligible observations only: a new observed low for a popular model, a daily drop of at least 15%, or a provider first observed after a prior-day baseline. Price types stay separate; adjacent observed calendar days are required for price comparisons.
growth_feed_limits: Retained daily observations only; coverage and providers may change. Not a continuous market series or a guarantee of stock. Spot may be interrupted; tax is excluded or unknown and fees may apply.
growth_drop: Price drop · at least 10% below the median of the previous 7 observed daily minima (same price type; all 7 days required)
note_aws: Official EC2 Linux shared-tenancy prices in two regions, refreshed daily. Spot entries are regional lowest prices, not availability-zone quotes; these floors do not set comparison headlines.
note_oracle: Official GPU-hour rate multiplied by the reviewed shape GPU count. OCPUs remain distinct from vCPUs. Region and inventory are unspecified.
note_ovh: Official FR subsidiary catalog in EUR, excluding VAT. Linux hourly instance prices; exact regions and capacity are unspecified. Local-zone and three-zone prices are not inferred.
note_vultr: Official hourly catalog with explicit GPU counts. Missing locations do not imply available capacity. Preemptible rates are labelled separately; unverified virtual GPU allocations are excluded.
note_hetzner: Public dedicated GPU servers, billed hourly with a monthly cap and an additional one-time setup fee. Configuration starting prices remain marked; display only.
note_gcp: Official Cloud Billing Catalog GPU-hour components, including A3/A2/G2 GPU SKUs. GPU only; VM vCPU/RAM billed separately. Collection skips when GCP_BILLING_API_KEY is absent; catalog attempts are limited to once per six hours. Capacity is unknown.

guide_index_intro: Understand GPU rental quotes before choosing a cloud provider. These guides combine source-linked explanations with the current database snapshot.
guide_choose_title: How to choose a GPU cloud for LLM inference
guide_choose_intro: Start with model memory, then compare the billable allocation, region and price type. A low GPU-hour rate alone does not establish whether a model fits or what the full instance costs.
guide_spot_intro: Compare observed Spot discounts within matching configurations. Cheaper interruptible capacity comes with service continuity risks; a discount is not a reliability or availability guarantee.
guide_billing_intro: Multi-GPU instances can have an attractive normalized rate and a much larger mandatory bill. Use the observed allocation and billing minimum to compare like for like.
guide_glossary_intro: Read the labels attached to each quote. These definitions describe the comparison policy and provider billing concepts; they do not replace a provider contract.
guide_value_title: Cheapest GPU per VRAM GB right now
guide_value_intro: Compare the lowest observed cost per GB of GPU memory per hour for each exact model and price type, with popular models first. This measures memory cost, not inference speed or overall value.
guide_basis: Current means eligible observations in this build’s dated database snapshot, not a new availability check or a market-wide minimum. Whole-GPU USD quotes only; standard and unspecified regions, tax excluded or unknown. Spot stays separate. Stale, fractional, advertised starting prices and GPU-only components do not enter the calculations. Source, tax, marketplace, FX and billing qualifiers remain on the offer cards.
guide_memory: The table computes ideal weight storage from nominal model-card parameter counts stored as database references. FP16 uses two bytes per parameter; packed four-bit weights use half a byte. Results are decimal GB, not GiB. These are nominal-size arithmetic estimates, not measured VRAM requirements: quantization metadata, KV cache, activations and runtime memory add overhead. Context length and concurrency change the requirement. Extra GPU memory does not prove throughput, and memory across multiple GPUs requires a supported sharding setup. Check the linked estimator and cache documentation before choosing capacity.
guide_choose_steps: Keep headroom above weight storage and test the intended context, batch and precision. The classes below are non-overlapping memory bands per GPU. Their cheapest observed quotes are a shortlist, not a recommendation or proof that a named model fits. Compare the linked exact-model and provider pages for allocation, location and source conditions.
guide_spot_method: Match the exact model, provider, SKU, region, GPU count, allocation fraction, scope, currency, tax basis, CPU, RAM and initial billing duration. For each matched pair compute the percentage reduction from on-demand to Spot, then take the median of those reductions per popular model. Negative values mean Spot was dearer. The two price medians describe the matched cohort; their ratio need not equal the median discount. No cross-provider or cross-region pairing; regional from-price floors are excluded. Sample counts measure matched configurations, not capacity or interruption probability.
guide_interruptions: AWS interruption notices are best effort and hibernation can begin immediately. Azure may evict Spot VMs when capacity is needed or the configured maximum price is exceeded. Google Cloud can reclaim Spot VMs and does not provide the same availability commitments as standard VMs. Plan checkpointing, retries and recovery, and check the official provider documentation linked below. These observations do not estimate interruption rates.
guide_billing_math: For an instance-scoped quote, divide the instance hourly price by its GPU count to obtain the normalized GPU-hour rate. For a per-GPU quote, multiply by the mandatory GPU count to obtain the instance hourly total. The initial compute charge is that total multiplied by the documented minimum billing duration as a fraction of an hour. The live examples retain both amounts and the documented duration. Unknown duration stays unknown.
guide_billing_limits: The minimum shown covers listed compute only. Storage, network transfer, platform fees and tax may add charges; unknown charges are not filled with zeros. GPU component quotes omit separately billed VM resources, so they cannot establish a whole-instance minimum. Provider billing increments and commitments vary; confirm the source before renting. A normalized rate does not mean individual GPUs can be rented separately.
guide_value_method: Divide the eligible USD price per GPU-hour by the explicit per-GPU GB capacity in the database model name. Choose the lowest observed rate for each exact model and price type; do not merge interfaces, capacities or laptop variants. Popular families appear first, then the other model names. GB and GiB are not interchanged, and an unspecified capacity has no ratio. Use the accompanying cards to compare mandatory instance totals, unknown stock and taxes before acting on a low ratio.
guide_term_demand: On-demand: usage billed without the term commitment of a reserved plan. The listed allocation and provider billing rules still apply; an hourly display does not establish the billing increment.
guide_term_spot: Spot, preemptible and interruptible: provider-specific ways to sell capacity that can be reclaimed. Names do not imply identical interruption or billing terms. This site keeps interruptible and reserved labels separate from the on-demand/Spot comparison population.
guide_term_reserved: Reserved: a commitment-based pricing arrangement. Term, payment schedule and capacity guarantees depend on the product. Do not infer that every reservation reserves physical capacity or compare an amortized commitment with cancellable hourly rental without a label.
guide_term_market: Community marketplace: capacity offered by independent hosts rather than a uniform provider fleet. Reliability and host location are not independently verified here. Marketplace stablecoin and platform-fee conditions remain visible; a USD label is not proof of a final fiat invoice.
guide_term_tax: Tax basis: included, excluded or unknown, as supported by the source. Unknown never means tax-free. The comparison population permits excluded and unknown tax bases, so displayed prices are not a uniform tax-inclusive checkout total.
guide_term_from: From-price: an advertised starting amount or sampled regional floor, not a specific deployable quote with guaranteed stock. It remains labelled in source displays and is excluded from these guide calculations.
guide_term_component: GPU component price: only the accelerator portion. VM CPU and memory can be billed separately. Without a verified full-machine composition, the instance total and initial minimum charge are unknown; component rates do not compete with whole-instance quotes.
guide_term_regions: Region classes: standard, restricted, edge and unspecified are comparison labels. They describe reviewed deployment identifiers, not provider headquarters. Restricted and edge rows stay outside these calculations. Unspecified remains unknown; unfamiliar identifiers default to standard under the site policy and require review, not an invented access guarantee.

guide_discount_caption: Discounts in the current matched observation cohort

report_index_intro: A weekly view of retained GPU cloud observations, with comparable prices, coverage changes and links to the underlying offers.
report_intro: This report summarizes observed GPU cloud prices for this ISO week. Current-week pages update as observations arrive; archived weeks use their last observed UTC day.
report_basis: Prices are USD per GPU-hour for whole GPUs in standard or unspecified regions. Exact on-demand and Spot rates stay separate. Starting prices, tax-included rates and GPU-component-only charges are excluded. Display-only sources retain their rights restrictions; availability and tax must be checked with the provider.
report_matching: Weekly changes use only groups present on both dates: the same provider, exact GPU model, GPU count, region, price type, currency, price scope, tax basis, billing terms, original currency and conditions. For each model and price type, we select the cheapest current matched group and compare its own previous minimum. This can differ from the unrestricted current minimum. Archived data stores group minima, not every SKU or machine; these are observed group-price changes, not guaranteed same-instance price cuts. Currency conversion can affect USD changes.
report_coverage: Coverage changes can move minima. Missing observations do not prove a provider closed or a GPU sold out. No dates or missing prices are filled in.
report_thin: Insufficient comparable history: this page is noindex until at least three popular model/price-type comparisons have both dates.
report_short: There is no eligible observation exactly one week earlier. Weekly changes and listing changes are unavailable; the current snapshot is shown without invented comparisons.
report_counts_note: Today counts eligible observed offers; archived dates count retained daily groups. Historical counts are not full catalog sizes and must not be interpreted as offer growth. Provider counts refer only to eligible observations.
report_units: USD / GPU-hour; price types are separate
report_moves: Biggest absolute percentage moves among the comparisons
report_empty: No eligible popular GPU price was observed.
report_no_comparisons: No like-for-like weekly comparison is available.
report_no_moves: No non-zero move is supported by the available comparisons.
report_listings_note: These are newly observed and no-longer-observed models/providers between the two snapshots, not confirmed launches or delistings. The initial import is not news. Missing or failed collections can explain disappearances; provider availability is unconfirmed.
report_feed_rules: The same feed also links to weekly reports with observed popular-GPU prices, including reports labelled as having insufficient weekly history. Comparisons use matched weekly groups and may include labelled display-only sources. Each week keeps a stable feed identifier.
